Then do what the epic needs within the latitude contract: plan waves, dispatch one Commander per issue (each in an isolated worktree, each with a completed templates/LAUNCH_ORDER.template.md carrying pasted prior-wave verdicts, pre-rulings, honest-null clause, findings-file assignment, stop conditions, and inherited latitude), adjudicate what Commanders float (inside delegated classes as logged RULINGs, otherwise escalate), merge green reviewed PRs sequentially gated on check exit codes, and stop at wave checkpoints per the contract. Treat forecast as provisional. At every wave boundary or material exception, write .agent-work/20260820-deficiency-cleanup/NEXT_WAVE.json with the exact boundary_id, launch_id, and trigger; consume exact ../constellation-replan/templates/REPLAN_INPUT.template.json and ../constellation-replan/templates/REPLAN_RESULT.template.json packets under .agent-work/20260820-deficiency-cleanup/transitions/<boundary-id>/; append exactly one '- TRANSITION | boundary=<boundary-id> | decision=<decision> | verified' line to ADMIRAL_LOG.md; and run python /home/tommy/projects/constellation-skills/scripts/verify_iterative_role_artifacts.py admiral-prelaunch --work-id 20260820-deficiency-cleanup in the foreground before any next launch. A nonzero result refuses launch. The verifier requires a unique advance|repair|replan|stop exit, enforces repair safety, and writes CURRENT_TRUTH.md plus WAVE_REVIEW.md from revised_epic_body and wave_review_comment. Planning makes no direct gh/network mutation; future posting goes only through the authorized tracker port after normal gates. Log every ruling, incident, wave launch, transition exit, merge, and owned error in the ADMIRAL_LOG as it happens — an unlogged ruling didn't happen. Never run a Commander's issue yourself; never put two Commanders in one worktree. If the contract expires, a fixed-boundary proposal exceeds latitude, or the ground shifts under it, surface a contract-refresh or human decision before continuing.

closeout.title: Lessons audit, reconcile, hygiene, acceptance
closeout.imperative: The run cannot close without a record of what happened. 1) Write the epic retrospective as EPISODES: one episode per distinct thing that happened across the epic — not one per wave, and not a summary — each stating its task-intent, expected-behavior, observed-behavior, impact-cost and workaround, and each harvesting what the ADMIRAL_LOG, the crew Workflow Feedback and the Commander returns actually recorded. An episode is a record, not a rule: write what you observed, and do NOT write a rule for a future agent to follow — a rule to follow belongs in docs/agents/* and is a human's call. Write the delta to .agent-work/20260820-deficiency-cleanup/episode-delta.json and apply it deterministically: python /home/tommy/projects/constellation-skills/scripts/apply_episode_delta.py --delta .agent-work/20260820-deficiency-cleanup/episode-delta.json --store-root episodes. Pass --store-root on every invocation: the writer's default resolves relative to the installed skill directory, so an installed copy would silently build a store at ~/.claude/skills/constellation-admiral/episodes — outside the repo — while every gate reported green. Never hand-edit a file under episodes/: that writer is the only write path into it. Then run the capture gate before advancing: python /home/tommy/projects/constellation-skills/scripts/verify_episode_captured.py 20260820-deficiency-cleanup --store-root episodes --phase feedback. 2) When any part of this closeout edits a shipped compact-format JSON template, edit the raw text surgically (never round-trip it through json.load/json.dump, which reflows the file and destroys blame) and re-validate with json.load afterward. 3) Hand the epic's net change to a constellation-cartographer subagent for architecture reconcile. 4) Hygiene: every branch merged or dispositioned, worktrees swept, ADMIRAL_LOG archived under .agent-work/archive/. 5) Present the epic summary and get user acceptance. Then release the lease: call the spine_lease MCP tool with action=release (your own spine; no session id argument needed).

The epic is complete and its chartered question is answered by retirement rather than by choice. Five implementation lanes plus the A+B display batch are merged to main at 373f08c3 with the ordinary suite green at 3472/6/1224; three of those lanes were blocked by independent review and repaired before approval. The architecture cluster was not designed: a channel experiment through run_crew --backend cli reproduced none of E1, E2, E3 or E5b, showing the authority half was an artifact of the Admiral's own dispatch channel, and the final ballot put minimal intervention and status quo above two of the three full designs. What the epic actually found is smaller and worse than what it was chartered to find — _is_stale existed, worked, and was called in four places, none of them a rendering path, so the engine printed LEASE active and 'you are 7 steps from done ... Run it.' over plans dead for weeks, and 58 of 58 active leases in this checkout were stale. That is fixed at both renderers and at SessionStart. Option C was investigated and found dominated rather than broken: the Stop guard is armed by the binding store written by the act of claim, not by the lease record, so demoting the lease would not deliver its own benefit. Every ledger item and related issue is dispositioned, three further defects are recorded as episodes rather than filed, and the residual is a human scoping decision on #615's two questions, not further execution under this contract.
